questions.title: What is the primary difference between Supervised and Unsupervised Learning?
options: A. Supervised learning requires more processing power
B. Supervised learning uses labeled data; Unsupervised learning finds patterns in unlabeled data
C. Unsupervised learning is only used for images
D. Supervised learning cannot be used for regression
questions.explanation: Supervised learning involves training a model on a dataset where the answer (label) is already known. Unsupervised learning looks for hidden structures or clusters within data that has no labels.
questions.source_text: What is the primary difference between Supervised and Unsupervised Learning?

questions.title: In Machine Learning, what is 'Overfitting'?
options: A. When a model is too simple to learn the underlying trend
B. When a model learns the training data and its noise too well, performing poorly on new data
C. When the dataset is too large for the computer's memory
D. When the model's accuracy is 0%
questions.explanation: Overfitting happens when a model becomes too complex and 'memorizes' the training data, losing its ability to generalize to unseen examples.
questions.source_text: In Machine Learning, what is 'Overfitting'?

B. Grouping customers based on purchasing habits
C. Determining if an email is 'Spam' or 'Not Spam'
D. Predicting the temperature for tomorrow
questions.explanation: Classification is about predicting a discrete label or category. Predicting a continuous numerical value (like price or temperature) is called 'Regression'.

C. To satisfy the requirements of the Python interpreter
D. To double the amount of data available

B. The average of the squared differences between predicted and actual values
C. The number of features used in the model
D. The time it takes to train the model

questions.title: What does 'Feature Scaling' (like Normalization or Standardization) help with?
options: A. It makes the dataset smaller to save space
B. It ensures all features contribute equally to the model, preventing variables with larger scales from dominating
C. It labels the data automatically
D. It removes outliers from the dataset

questions.title: What is the 'Bias-Variance Tradeoff'?

B. The balance between a model being too simple (high bias) vs. too sensitive to noise (high variance)
C. The cost of buying more GPUs for training
D. The difference between training time and prediction time
questions.explanation: A good model finds the 'sweet spot' where both bias and variance are minimized to achieve the lowest possible total error on new data.
questions.source_text: What is the 'Bias-Variance Tradeoff'?

questions.company_tags: 通用,技术岗,校招线上测评,ai-rag,data-analysis
questions.title: In a binary classification Confusion Matrix, what is a 'False Positive'?
options: A. When the model predicts 0 and the actual value is 0
B. When the model predicts 1 but the actual value is 0
C. When the model fails to make any prediction
D. When the model correctly identifies a negative case
questions.explanation: A False Positive (Type I error) occurs when the model incorrectly predicts the positive class (e.g., diagnosing a healthy patient with a disease).
questions.source_text: In a binary classification Confusion Matrix, what is a 'False Positive'?

questions.company_tags: 通用,技术岗,校招线上测评,ai-rag,data-analysis

options: A. The process of cleaning the training data

C. Automatically writing code for the neural network
D. Updating the weights of a model during training
questions.explanation: Hyperparameters are settings defined before training (like learning rate or number of trees). 'Tuning' (e.g., GridSearch) finds the best combination of these settings.
questions.source_text: What is 'Hyperparameter Tuning'?

questions.company_tags: 通用,技术岗,校招线上测评,ai-rag,data-analysis
questions.title: What does 'Accuracy' measure in a classification model?
options: A. The number of positive predictions made
B. The ratio of correctly predicted observations to the total observations
C. The speed at which the model makes a prediction
D. The difference between the highest and lowest scores
questions.explanation: Accuracy is the most intuitive performance measure, but it can be misleading if the dataset is imbalanced (e.g., 99% of cases are Class A).
questions.source_text: What does 'Accuracy' measure in a classification model?

questions.company_tags: 通用,技术岗,校招线上测评,ai-rag,data-analysis
questions.title: In a medical test, what does 'Recall' (Sensitivity) represent?
options: A. The ability of the model to find all the positive cases
B. The ability of the model to avoid false alarms
C. The total number of patients tested
D. The time it takes to get results
questions.explanation: Recall answers: 'Of all the people who actually had the disease, how many did we correctly identify?' High recall is critical when the cost of a False Negative is high.
questions.source_text: In a medical test, what does 'Recall' (Sensitivity) represent?

questions.company_tags: 通用,技术岗,校招线上测评,ai-rag,data-analysis
questions.title: What is 'Precision'?
options: A. The total number of correct predictions
B. The ratio of correctly predicted positive observations to the total predicted positives
C. The consistency of the model over time
D. The depth of the neural network
questions.explanation: Precision answers: 'Of all the people we labeled as having the disease, how many actually had it?' High precision is critical when the cost of a False Positive is high (e.g., spam filters).
questions.source_text: What is 'Precision'?

questions.company_tags: 通用,技术岗,校招线上测评,ai-rag,data-analysis
questions.title: What is the 'F1-Score'?
options: A. The maximum accuracy a model can reach
B. The harmonic mean of Precision and Recall
C. The square root of the Mean Squared Error
D. The ratio of training data to testing data
questions.explanation: The F1-Score provides a balance between Precision and Recall. It is particularly useful when you have an uneven class distribution.
questions.source_text: What is the 'F1-Score'?

questions.company_tags: 通用,技术岗,校招线上测评,ai-rag,data-analysis
questions.title: What does the 'ROC Curve' (Receiver Operating Characteristic) visualize?
options: A. The distribution of features in the dataset
B. The trade-off between the True Positive Rate and the False Positive Rate at various thresholds
C. The decrease in loss over training epochs
D. The relationship between two independent variables
questions.explanation: The ROC curve helps in choosing the best threshold for a classifier. A model with an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 1.0 is perfect.
questions.source_text: What does the 'ROC Curve' (Receiver Operating Characteristic) visualize?

questions.company_tags: 通用,技术岗,校招线上测评,ai-rag,data-analysis

D. Training the model on K different computers at once

questions.company_tags: 通用,技术岗,校招线上测评,ai-rag,data-analysis
questions.title: What is the 'Area Under the Precision-Recall Curve' (PR-AUC) often preferred over ROC-AUC?
options: A. When the model is a neural network
B. When dealing with highly imbalanced datasets where the minority class is the focus
C. When the dataset has more than 1,000 features
D. When the labels are continuous numbers

questions.source_text: What is the 'Area Under the Precision-Recall Curve' (PR-AUC) often preferred over ROC-AUC?

questions.company_tags: 通用,技术岗,校招线上测评,ai-rag,data-analysis
questions.title: What does 'MAE' (Mean Absolute Error) measure?
